mainTopic: The full brother and son status of a ממזר, and whether a sister who is also the father's wife's daughter brings one חיוב or two.
overview: The amud finishes the earlier point that a ממזר brother also creates the bond of יבום. It then explains the משנה's words 'he is his brother in all respects': he inherits, and a כהן may become impure for him. That is true even though a כהן may not become impure for an unfit wife, because a wife is meant to be sent away but a brother stays a brother. A brother from a שפחה or a גויה does not count at all, because the child follows the mother. Any son, even a ממזר, frees his father's widow from יבום, learned from 'ובן אין לו'. A ממזר son is punished for hitting his father when the father has done תשובה, even though his sin can never be fully fixed. Then a ברייתא brings an argument between the רבנן and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: does a sister who is also his father's wife's daughter bring two חיובים or one? Along the way the amud teaches אין מזהירין מן הדין, and that a half-sister counts only if her mother could legally marry the father. רבא's teaching shows that a sister born to an אנוסה still counts.

steps.title: A ממזר brother also creates the levirate bond
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier discussion: a brother who is a ממזר also creates a levirate bond (זיקה) with his dead brother's widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also creates the levirate bond.
steps.whatsHappening: This short line closes the earlier discussion. A brother who is a ממזר also ties his brother's widow to him for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that any kind of brother counts for יבום. This line confirms that a ממזר brother is included in that bond. His flawed lineage does not cancel the brother relationship.

keyTerms.meaning: Ties or binds; here it means creating the levirate bond
The levirate bond between the widow and her dead husband's brother
A child born from a forbidden union, whose lineage is flawed
Levirate marriage, when a brother marries his childless brother's widow

phrases.english: He also creates the levirate bond.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the brother who is a ממזר, from the discussion just before this line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from before this section, on whether a ממזר brother counts for יבום.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A ממזר brother creates זיקה just like any other brother.

steps.title: What does 'his brother in all respects' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'he is his brother in all respects' and asks which laws it refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he is his brother in every respect.' For which law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה and asks what 'in all respects' adds. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said that a brother of any kind, even a ממזר, creates the bond for יבום. 'In all respects' sounds like it covers even more. The גמרא wants to know exactly which other laws are meant.

keyTerms.meaning: In all respects, for every matter
For which law? What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: And he is his brother in every respect.
For which law is this said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יבום point to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical laws the phrase 'his brother in all respects' covers.

steps.title: He inherits, and a כהן becomes impure for him
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ממזר brother inherits from his brother, and a כהן may become impure to bury him.
steps.simpleTranslation: To inherit from him, and to become impure for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'in all respects' means two things. He inherits from his brother, and a כהן brother may become טמא at his funeral.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן normally may not become טמא from a dead body, but he may do so for close relatives, and a brother is one of them. The phrase teaches that a ממזר brother is included in both inheritance and this permission.

keyTerms.meaning: To become ritually impure for him, by attending his burial
A priest, who may become impure only for close relatives

phrases.english: To inherit from him, and to become impure for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase covers inheritance and a כהן's permission to become impure for his ממזר brother.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: he is his brother, so of course these laws apply. Why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious? He is his brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for saying something that seems obvious. If he really is a brother, why spell out that he inherits and that a כהן may become impure for him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the classic פשיטא challenge. A משנה should not waste words, so the גמרא looks for a reason someone might have thought otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! Why say it?

phrases.english: Isn't this obvious? He is his brother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement 'he is his brother in all respects'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A brother is a brother, so these laws should apply automatically. Saying it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: We might have compared him to an unfit wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it is not obvious. A כהן may become impure for a fit wife but not an unfit one, so we might have thought the same about a fit brother and an unfit one. The משנה teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since it is written 'except for his kin that is near to him,' and 'his kin' means his wife, and it is also written 'a husband shall not become impure among his people to profane himself,' there must be a husband who becomes impure and one who does not. He becomes impure for a fit wife but not for an unfit wife. So too, he would become impure for a fit brother but not for an unfit one. The משנה teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the פשיטא. It shows that the פסוקים split wives into fit and unfit, so we might have split brothers the same way, and the משנה is needed to reject that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק allows a כהן to become impure for his wife ('שארו'), and another says a husband may not. The two are reconciled by saying the permission is only for a wife he was allowed to marry. Without the משנה we would have applied the same fit/unfit split to a ממזר brother.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say (introduces a mistaken idea)
His kin; here explained as his wife
How so? How do we reconcile this?
Unfit; here a wife forbidden to a כהן, or a brother of flawed lineage
It teaches us (that the mistaken idea is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as the conclusion. Everything from סלקא דעתך until קא משמע לן is the mistaken idea the משנה comes to reject.

phrases.english: You might have thought to say:
since it is written:
"except for his kin that is near to him,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:2

phrases.english: and the Master said: "his kin" means his wife,
and it is written: "A husband shall not become impure among his people, to profane himself,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:4. This seems to clash with the פסוק that lets him become impure for his wife.

phrases.english: so there is a husband who becomes impure
and there is a husband who does not become impure.
How so?
He becomes impure for his wife who is fit,
but he does not become impure for his wife who is unfit,
phrases.notes: An unfit wife is one a כהן was not allowed to marry.

phrases.english: so too here:
he would become impure for a fit brother,
but not for an unfit brother.
So the משנה teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 4 by showing a real reason to think otherwise.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הוה אמינא (מהו דתימא style): shows there was a real reason to think the opposite.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Just as a כהן may not become impure for an unfit wife, he may not become impure for an unfit (ממזר) brother.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that a כהן does become impure for his ממזר brother.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the fit/unfit split for wives comes from reading two פסוקים together. It is not a general rule for every relative.

steps.title: Maybe the comparison is correct
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the comparison to an unfit wife is actually right, and a כהן should not become impure for an unfit brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us say it is so here too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Why reject the comparison? Maybe a כהן really should not become impure for an unfit brother, just like an unfit wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הוה אמינא sounded reasonable. Now the גמרא asks why it should be wrong, which requires showing a real difference between a wife and a brother.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us say it is so here too

phrases.english: But let us say it is so here too!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe a כהן truly may not become impure for an unfit brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of the הוה אמינא in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that a כהן becomes impure for his ממזר brother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison to an unfit wife seems valid, so the law for brothers should follow it.

steps.title: A wife can be sent away, but a brother stays a brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the difference. An unfit wife is supposed to be divorced, so she is not truly his kin. A brother is always his brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, she stands to be sent away. Here, he is his brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the comparison fails. An unfit wife is supposed to be divorced, while a brother remains a brother no matter what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's marriage to an unfit wife is a bond that should be ended, so it does not earn him permission to become impure. A brother is related by birth, and that cannot be undone. So the ממזר brother keeps the full status of a brother.

keyTerms.meaning: She stands to be sent away (divorced)
There / here; used to contrast two cases

steps.whatToRemember: A ממזר brother is a full brother. He inherits, and a כהן may become impure for him. The unfit-wife rule does not apply, because a wife can be sent away but a brother is always a brother.

phrases.english: There, she stands to be sent away;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the unfit wife, whom he is supposed to divorce.

phrases.english: here, he is his brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by showing how a wife and a brother differ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An unfit brother should be treated like an unfit wife.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unfit wife is meant to be divorced, so she loses the status of kin, but a brother's relationship is permanent.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן becomes impure for his ממזר brother, because the brother relationship cannot be undone.

steps.title: The exception: a brother from a maidservant or a gentile woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a brother born from a שפחה or a גויה does not count as a brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: except for someone whose brother was born from a maidservant or from a gentile woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, which list an exception to the rule that a brother of any kind counts. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, even an unfit brother like a ממזר was fully a brother. Here the משנה says there is one group that is not counted as a brother at all: a son of a שפחה or of a גויה.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not like the ממזר. A ממזר is a real brother who is just unfit to marry into the community. A son of a שפחה or a גויה does not count as the father's family at all.

phrases.english: Except for whoever has a brother
from a maidservant or from a gentile woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מִמִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אָח מִן הַשִּׁפְחָה וּמִן הַגּוֹיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the ממזר brother discussion to the משנה's exception clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brother born from a שפחה or a גויה is not considered a brother.

steps.title: Asking for the reason behind the exception
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the source is for not counting such a brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a brother from a שפחה or a גויה does not count. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The father is the same man, so the גמרא wants to know what makes this son different. It is looking for a source.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the exception just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for why a son of a שפחה or a גויה is not counted as his father's family.

steps.title: The child follows the mother
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the children of a שפחה belong to her master, so the child takes the mother's status, not the father's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The wife and her children shall belong to her master.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that says the children of a שפחה belong to her master, just as she does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the children belong to the master, they share the mother's status and are not counted as part of the father's family. So such a son is not his father's son, and he is not a brother to the father's other sons.
steps.whatToRemember: A child of a שפחה or a גויה takes the mother's status, so he is not counted as a brother at all.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"The wife and her children shall be her master's."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:4

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: הָאִשָּׁה וִילָדֶיהָ תִּהְיֶה לַאדוֹנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her children belong to the master, which shows the child follows the mother's status and not the father's.

steps.title: A son of any kind frees the widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a man with a son of any kind frees his wife from יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: someone who has a son of any kind frees his father's wife from יבום, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about sons. This sets up a question about the words 'of any kind'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום only happens when a man dies without children. The משנה says any son at all frees the widow, so there is no יבום and no חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Of any kind / in any case

phrases.english: Whoever has a son
of any kind exempts, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה says he frees his father's wife from יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּן מִכׇּל מָקוֹם פּוֹטֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the brother section of the משנה to the son section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any son exempts the father's wife from יבום.

steps.title: What does 'of any kind' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of son the words 'of any kind' come to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'of any kind' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what extra case the words 'of any kind' are meant to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just said 'a son.' Adding 'of any kind' suggests it means to include a son we might have thought does not count.

phrases.english: "Of any kind" comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which son is included by the extra words 'of any kind'.

steps.title: It includes a ממזר son
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the words come to include a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: it comes to include a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that 'of any kind' means even a ממזר son frees the widow from יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר is unfit to marry into the community, so we might have thought he does not count as a son. רב יהודה says he does count, and the widow is free.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden relationship (such as עריות)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It comes to include a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'of any kind'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ממזר son also counts and exempts the widow.

steps.title: Source: 'ובן אין לו' means check carefully
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ובן אין לו' is read as 'עיין עליו', so we must check whether he has any child at all, even a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says 'and he has no son', which is read as 'investigate him'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רב יהודה's rule by reading the words of the יבום פסוק in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אין לו' sound like 'עיין עליו', investigate him. This teaches that we must check whether he has any child at all. If he has any son, even a ממזר, there is no יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: And he has no son (the יבום פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: Any son, even a ממזר, frees the widow from יבום, learned from 'אין לו' read as 'עיין עליו'.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
As the verse states: "And he has no son"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: investigate him.
phrases.notes: A play on sounds: 'אין לו' is read like 'עיין עליו', so look into whether he has any child at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּאָמַר קְרָא: וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's answer with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That a ממזר son exempts from יבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 25:5, 'ובן אין לו', read as 'עיין עליו'.

steps.title: The ממזר son is punished for hitting his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the son, even a ממזר, is liable for striking his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and he is liable for hitting him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a ממזר son is punished for striking his father. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the ממזר as a full son here too. If he hits his father, he gets the full punishment for hitting a parent.

phrases.english: And he is liable for striking him.
phrases.notes: This is the ממזר son hitting his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next ruling in the same משנה line about sons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזר son is liable for striking his father.

steps.title: Why protect a father who sinned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the son is liable, since the protection applies only to someone who acts like a proper member of the people, and this father sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Apply here the פסוק 'Do not curse a leader among your people', which protects only someone who acts the way your people should.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. A father who had a ממזר did a serious sin, so why should his son be punished for hitting him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בעמך', among your people, are taken to mean that the protection only covers someone who behaves like a proper member of the nation. To have a ממזר, the father must have been with a forbidden woman. So it seems he loses this protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Read here, apply this פסוק here
One who acts the way your people should

phrases.english: Why?
Read here:
"You shall not curse a ruler of your people,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:27

phrases.english: only for one who acts according to the deeds of your people!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? קְרִי כָּאן: וְנָשִׂיא בְעַמְּךָ לֹא תָאוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה ruling just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a ממזר son is liable for striking his father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Protection applies only to one who acts like 'your people'. A father who fathered a ממזר sinned, so he should not be protected.

steps.title: The father did תשובה
steps.stepSummary: Using רב פנחס's answer in the name of רב פפא, the גמרא says the case is a father who did תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב פנחס said in the name of רב פפא: it is talking about someone who did תשובה. Here too, it is when the father did תשובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a father who did תשובה after the ממזר was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father does תשובה, he again acts like a proper member of the people. So the פסוק's protection applies to him again, and the son is liable for hitting him. The גמרא borrows this answer from רב פנחס, who used it in a different case.
steps.whatToRemember: A ממזר son is liable for hitting his father when the father has done תשובה, because then the father again counts as one who acts like 'your people'.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a sinner never gets protection in any case. It explains the משנה as a case where the father did תשובה.

phrases.english: As Rav Pinchas said
in the name of Rav Pappa:
It refers to one who repents;
here too, it is when he repented.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב פִּנְחָס מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא: בְּעוֹשֶׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by limiting the משנה's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the father did תשובה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father sinned, so he loses the protection of 'בעמך' and the son should not be liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a father who did תשובה, so he counts as 'עושה מעשה עמך' again and the son is liable.

steps.title: Can a father of a ממזר really do תשובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 17's answer, citing שמעון בן מנסיא: one who fathered a ממזר is 'crooked that cannot be made straight.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Can this man really do תשובה? Didn't we learn: שמעון בן מנסיא says, what is 'the crooked that cannot be made straight'? This is a man who had relations with a forbidden relative and fathered a ממזר from her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It says the father did תשובה, but a source says a man who fathered a ממזר cannot fix what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 solved the problem by saying the father did תשובה. שמעון בן מנסיא reads 'מעוות לא יוכל לתקון' as being about exactly this man. The ממזר child exists forever, so it seems his sin can never be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: The crooked cannot be made straight (קהלת)

phrases.english: And is this one capable of repentance?
But didn't we learn:
Shimon ben Menasya says:
Which is 'That which is crooked cannot be made straight'?
phrases.notes: קהלת 1:15

phrases.english: This is one who has relations with a forbidden relative
and fathered a ממזר from her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case is a father who did תשובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמעון בן מנסיא says a man who fathered a ממזר is 'crooked that cannot be made straight,' so his תשובה seems impossible.

steps.title: At least now he acts like a proper member of the people
steps.stepSummary: Even if he cannot fully fix the sin, after תשובה he now counts as 'עושה מעשה עמך,' so his son is liable for hitting him.
steps.simpleTranslation: At least now he is someone who acts according to the deeds of your people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the father may not be able to undo the ממזר. Still, his תשובה means that right now he behaves like a proper Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמעון בן מנסיא meant the sin can't be completely repaired. The law about hitting a parent only requires that the father currently be 'עושה מעשה עמך,' and his תשובה is enough for that. So the son is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Acts according to the deeds of your people, meaning he behaves like a proper Jew

steps.whatToRemember: A son, even a ממזר, is liable for hitting his father. That holds when the father did תשובה: even though he cannot undo the ממזר, he now counts as 'עושה מעשה עמך.'

phrases.english: At least now
he acts according to the deeds of your people.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא עוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֵׂה עַמְּךָ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what is required: full repair is not needed, only present good conduct.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the sin can't be undone, his תשובה doesn't count, and he is not 'עושה מעשה עמך.'
steps.terutzMaskana: His תשובה makes him 'עושה מעשה עמך' now, even if the sin itself stays 'crooked.'

steps.title: Sister who is also father's wife's daughter: one חיוב or two?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the רבנן say he is liable twice, once for 'sister' and once for 'father's wife's daughter.' רבי יוסי בן יהודה says only once, for 'sister.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: one who has relations with his sister, and she is the daughter of his father's wife, is liable because of 'his sister' and because of 'his father's wife's daughter.' רבי יוסי בן יהודה says: he is liable only because of 'his sister,' and not because of 'his father's wife's daughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. Two opinions argue about whether one act with this woman counts as one sin or two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman is one person who fits two Torah descriptions: his sister, and the daughter of his father's wife. The רבנן count two separate prohibitions. רבי יוסי בן יהודה counts only the sister prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of his father's wife

steps.confusionAlert: There is only one woman here. The argument is whether this one woman brings two separate prohibitions or just one.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who has relations with his sister,
and she is the daughter of his father's wife
is liable because of 'his sister'
and because of 'his father's wife's daughter.'
Rabbi Yosei ben Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם אֲחוֹתוֹ בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: He is liable only because of 'his sister' alone,
and not because of 'his father's wife's daughter.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: two חיובים. רבי יוסי בן יהודה: only one, for 'sister.'

steps.title: What is the רבנן's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the רבנן's view that there are two חיובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the רבנן get the idea of two separate prohibitions. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack. It asks for the פסוק behind the ruling, and the answer will come from an extra פסוק in the Torah.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source for the רבנן's two חיובים

steps.title: The extra פסוק teaches a second חיוב
steps.stepSummary: The Torah already forbade a sister in ויקרא 18:9. The extra פסוק about the father's wife's daughter in 18:11 must teach a separate חיוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Since it is written, 'The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother,' why do I need 'The nakedness of your father's wife's daughter, born to your father, she is your sister'? Learn from this that he is liable because of 'his sister' and because of 'his father's wife's daughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second פסוק seems unnecessary, since a sister was already forbidden. So it must be adding a second prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every father's daughter is already covered by the first פסוק. A פסוק that forbids the father's wife's daughter adds nothing new about the act itself. So the רבנן learn that it creates its own separate חיוב.

phrases.english: They said:
Since it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״עֶרְוַת אֲחוֹתְךָ בַת אָבִיךָ אוֹ בַת אִמֶּךָ״,
phrases.english: 'The nakedness of your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:9

phrases.english: 'The nakedness of your father's wife's daughter,
born to your father, she is your sister'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:11

phrases.english: why do I need it?
Learn from this
to make him liable because of 'his sister'
and because of 'his father's wife's daughter.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seemingly extra פסוק (ויקרא 18:11) teaches a separate חיוב for 'father's wife's daughter.'

steps.title: רבי יוסי: 'She is your sister' limits it to one חיוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה reads the words 'אחותך היא' as a limit: he is liable for 'sister' only, not a second time for 'father's wife's daughter.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי בר יהודה? The פסוק says, 'she is your sister.' You make him liable because of 'his sister,' and you do not make him liable because of 'his father's wife's daughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's view. The same פסוק ends with 'she is your sister,' and he reads this as saying the prohibition is only about being a sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use the extra פסוק to add a second חיוב. רבי יוסי focuses on its closing words, 'אחותך היא.' To him they mean the only חיוב here is the sister one, so there is no second count.

keyTerms.meaning: You do not make him liable

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the same פסוק (ויקרא 18:11). The רבנן: its extra mention of the father's wife's daughter adds a second חיוב. רבי יוסי בר יהודה: its words 'אחותך היא' limit it to one חיוב, for 'sister.'

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking where he learns this from. He's the same רבי יוסי בן יהודה from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'she is your sister.'
Because of 'his sister' you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם בַּת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו.
phrases.english: and you do not make him liable because of 'his father's wife's daughter.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second opinion in the ברייתא, in contrast to Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'אחותך היא' limit the חיוב to the sister prohibition only.

steps.title: What do the Rabbis do with 'she is your sister'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן use the words 'אחותך היא', since they do not read them as a limit the way רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this 'אחותך היא'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the words 'אחותך היא'. This sets up the next step, where it gives their use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה used these words to limit the punishment to one חיוב. The רבנן hold there are two חיובים, so they cannot read the words as a limit. The words must still teach something, and the גמרא wants to know what.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (How do they use this פסוק?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this "she is your sister"
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״אֲחוֹתְךָ הִיא״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the derivation in step 23 back on the רבנן: if they do not use the words as a limit, what do they use them for?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the רבנן learn from the words 'אחותך היא'.

steps.title: The Rabbis use it to teach that we do not punish from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use 'אחותך היא' to punish a sister who is both his father's and his mother's daughter. This teaches that a punishment cannot be created from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to make him liable for his sister who is the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother. It teaches that we do not give a warning (and punishment) from a logical argument.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן need these words for a sister who is from both the same father and the same mother. The Torah spells this case out to teach that a קל וחומר cannot create a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might reason: if a half-sister from the father is forbidden, and a half-sister from the mother is forbidden, then surely a full sister is forbidden. That is a קל וחומר. The Torah writes the full-sister case anyway, to show that this kind of logic alone cannot make someone punishable. This is the rule of אין מזהירין מן הדין.

keyTerms.meaning: His full sister, the daughter of both his father and his mother
We do not create a warning or punishment from a logical argument (a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: אין מזהירין מן הדין is a basic rule across all of שס: a punishment must come from a פסוק, not from logic alone.

phrases.english: They need it to make him liable

phrases.aramaic: עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ בַּת אָבִיו וּבַת אִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: for his sister who is his father's daughter and his mother's daughter,
to say that we do not warn based on logic.
phrases.notes: 'מן הדין' here means from a קל וחומר. A 'warning' is what makes a person punishable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְחַיְּיבוֹ עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ בַּת אָבִיו וּבַת אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'אחותך היא' for a full sister. This teaches that we cannot punish based on a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: 'your sister' alone would be enough, so 'she is' teaches the limit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argues that for the רבנן's lesson the Torah only needed 'אחותך'. The extra word 'היא' must teach that he is liable only once, as a sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: If so, let the Torah write only 'your sister'. Why do I need 'she is'? To teach: you make him liable because of 'your sister', and you do not make him liable because of 'his father's wife's daughter'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה pushes back on the רבנן. He says their lesson only needs the word 'אחותך', so the extra word 'היא' must be teaching his limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fight is now over one small word, 'היא'. 'אחותך' alone is enough to teach the full-sister case and the קל וחומר rule. So 'היא' is extra, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads it as limiting: she counts as 'sister' only, with no second חיוב for 'father's wife's daughter'.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reading were right)
Let the Merciful One (the Torah) write
Why do I need it? (this word seems extra)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִם כֵּן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda: if so,
let the Merciful One write "your sister";
why do I need "she is"?
Because of "your sister" you make him liable,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בַּת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו״.
phrases.english: and you do not make him liable because of "his father's wife's daughter."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״אֲחוֹתְךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן's use of the פסוק from step 25 and defends his own reading from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's claim that 'אחותך היא' as a whole teaches אין מזהירין מן הדין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their lesson only needs 'אחותך'. The word 'היא' is left over, so it must teach the limit: one חיוב only.

steps.title: Rabbis: 'she is' is still needed for a general rule
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that even with 'אחותך' written, 'היא' is needed. Without it, you might think that in general we do punish from a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: Even though 'your sister' is written, it was necessary to write 'she is', so that you would not say that in general we warn based on a logical argument.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן defend themselves. They say the word 'היא' is not extra, because it is what turns the lesson into a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן agree that 'אחותך' alone covers the full-sister case. Their point is that 'היא' is what makes this a general rule for all of Torah: no punishments from a קל וחומר. The next step explains why 'אחותך' alone would not have been enough to teach that.

keyTerms.meaning: In general, in all other cases

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: even though "your sister" is written,
it was necessary to write "she is,"

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תֹּאמַר בְּעָלְמָא מַזְהִירִין מִן הַדִּין,
phrases.english: so that you not say that in general we warn based on logic,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן: אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתִיב ״אֲחוֹתְךָ״, אִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב ״הִיא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's challenge from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the 'extra' word has its own job: it turns the lesson into a general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'היא' is extra, so it must teach רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'היא' is needed so that we know, in general, we may not punish from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Why 'your sister' alone would not teach the rule
steps.stepSummary: Without 'היא', you could brush off 'אחותך' as the Torah simply spelling out something a קל וחומר already teaches. So the Torah added 'היא' to make the rule clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you would ask: why do I need 'your sister' that the Torah wrote? You could answer: it is something that could come from a קל וחומר, and the verse just took the trouble to write it anyway. That is why the Torah wrote 'she is'.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן explain why 'אחותך' alone would not have been enough. Someone could explain it away as the Torah writing out something it did not strictly need to, so the Torah added 'היא' to block that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah sometimes writes out a law that a קל וחומר could have taught, just to be extra clear. If only 'אחותך' were written, you could say that is all that happened here, and still use a קל וחומר to punish in other cases. The added 'היא' shows the Torah is making a real point: punishment needs a פסוק, not a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that could be learned from a קל וחומר
The verse took the trouble and wrote it anyway

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: 'אחותך היא' teaches אין מזהירין מן הדין, and 'היא' makes it a general rule. They learn the two חיובים from the extra פסוק itself (step 22). רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: 'היא' limits it to one חיוב, as a sister only.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Why do I need אחותך? It's a case of the Torah writing out a קל וחומר' is not the רבנן's real view. It is the mistaken way of reading the פסוק that the word 'היא' comes to block.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: ״אֲחוֹתְךָ״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: For if you would say: why do I need "your sister" that the Merciful One wrote?
[You might answer:] a matter that comes from a קל וחומר,
the verse took the trouble and wrote it anyway —
phrases.notes: This is the brush-off answer someone might give. It would leave the rule against punishing from a קל וחומר unproven.

phrases.english: [so] the Merciful One wrote "she is."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: ״אֲחוֹתְךָ״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the רבנן's answer in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Blocks a possible way of explaining away 'אחותך', showing why the extra word 'היא' is needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אחותך' alone could be read as the Torah simply writing out something a קל וחומר already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'היא' shows the Torah is teaching a real rule: we never punish from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: רבי יוסי asks why the words were not written in the other verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה pushes back on the רבנן. If 'אחותך היא' were there to punish for a full sister, it should have been written in the פסוק about a sister from father or mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה answers: If that is so, the Torah should have written 'she is your sister' in the other פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rejects the רבנן's reading of 'אחותך היא'. He says the words sit in the wrong place for the lesson the רבנן want to learn from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said 'אחותך היא' teaches the punishment for a sister who is both his father's and his mother's daughter. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says that lesson belongs in the פסוק that already mentions 'your father's daughter or your mother's daughter' (ויקרא 18:9). Since the words appear instead in the פסוק about 'בת אשת אביך', they must teach something else, namely his limit that he is punished only once.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah (the Merciful One) write it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda [answers]:
If so, let the Merciful One write
"she is your sister" in the other verse.
phrases.notes: The other פסוק is ויקרא 18:9, about a sister from your father or from your mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה responds to the רבנן's answer from steps 27-28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's use of 'אחותך היא' to teach the punishment for a full sister
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the purpose, the words would appear in ויקרא 18:9, which already speaks of a sister from father or mother. Their placement points to a different lesson.

steps.title: What does רבי יוסי learn from 'daughter of your father's wife'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses the words 'בת אשת אביך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, what does he do with this phrase 'the daughter of your father's wife'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from the words 'בת אשת אביך'. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses 'אחותך היא' for his own limit. The גמרא now checks that the nearby words 'בת אשת אביך' also have a job in his view, since the Torah does not waste words.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (How does he use this phrase?)
The daughter of your father's wife

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
this "daughter of your father's wife"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:11

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״בַּת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיךָ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses 'אחותך היא', the גמרא asks about another phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from 'בת אשת אביך'

steps.title: The sister's mother must be a woman the father could marry
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה needs 'בת אשת אביך' to teach that the sister counts only if her mother could legally marry the father. That excludes a sister from a שפחה or a גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to teach: only a sister whose mother your father could marry. This excludes his sister from a maidservant or a non-Jewish woman, whom your father cannot marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'אשת אביך' teaches that the sister's mother must be someone the father could legally marry. A half-sister from a שפחה or a גויה is therefore not counted as his sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is whether marriage could take effect between the father and the mother, not whether they actually married. With a שפחה or a גויה, קידושין cannot take effect at all, so the child is not legally his father's daughter for this איסור.

phrases.english: He needs it [to teach]:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִישׁוּת לְאָבִיךָ בָּהּ,
phrases.english: one whose mother your father can have marriage with,
excluding his sister from a maidservant or a non-Jewish woman,
with whom your father can have no marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אִישׁוּת לְאָבִיךָ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בת אשת אביך' limits the איסור to a sister whose mother could marry the father, excluding a sister from a שפחה or a גויה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a half-sister's status depends on whether her mother's union with the father could be a legal marriage.

steps.title: Why not exclude a sister from a raped woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading 'אשת אביך' more strictly: maybe it excludes even a sister born to an אנוסה, since her mother was never married to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: it excludes his sister from a woman who was raped?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. 'Your father's wife' might mean an actual wife, which would leave out a sister from an אנוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 read 'wife' as 'someone who could be a wife'. The challenge asks why we do not read 'wife' literally, as a woman actually married to the father. An אנוסה could have married him but did not, so this reading would exclude her daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was raped (taken by force, not married)

phrases.english: But say:
it excludes his sister from a woman who was raped?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how widely step 31 reads 'אשת אביך'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'אשת אביך' as 'a woman who could marry your father'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, 'wife' means an actual wife. That would exclude a sister from an אנוסה, who was never married to the father.

steps.title: רבא's teaching rules out that reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that you cannot exclude a sister from an אנוסה, because of a teaching of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that, because of רבא's teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge and points to רבא as the reason. The next step quotes רבא's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on רבא. He shows that the פסוק about 'your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter' is speaking about a woman the man raped. So a man's own children from an אנוסה count as his real family, and a sister born to the father's אנוסה cannot be excluded.

phrases.english: That you cannot say
because of [the teaching of] Rava,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32 by pointing to רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to an outside teaching (רבא's derivation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אשת אביך' might exclude a sister born from an אנוסה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's derivation shows that relationships through an אנוסה count, so her daughter is not excluded.

steps.title: רבא's contradiction between two verses about granddaughters
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out two פסוקים that seem to clash. One implies a woman's own granddaughters are permitted, and the other forbids them. He asks how to settle this.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא pointed out a contradiction. It is written: 'Do not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter.' That implies her own son's daughter and her own daughter's daughter are permitted. But it is also written: 'Do not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter, her son's daughter and her daughter's daughter.' How can this be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבא, who sets two פסוקים against each other. This is setup: רבא's answer, which proves the point about the אנוסה, comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 18:10 forbids 'your' granddaughters, which seems to imply that the woman's granddaughters from another man are allowed. ויקרא 18:17 forbids exactly those granddaughters of the woman. The question 'הא כיצד' asks how both can be true, and the answer will show how relatives through an אנוסה are treated.

keyTerms.meaning: How can this be? (How do we settle the contradiction?)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא's question is not the final point. Its answer, which comes next, is what proves that a sister from an אנוסה is still counted as his sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching of רבא mentioned in step 33.
steps.raayaObject: That a sister from an אנוסה is not excluded by 'אשת אביך'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's contradiction between ויקרא 18:10 and ויקרא 18:17, which he answers in step 35

steps.title: One verse speaks of rape, the other of marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבא settles the clash between the two פסוקים. The verse that implies a woman's granddaughters are permitted speaks about אונסין. The verse that forbids them speaks about נשואין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, it is talking about a woman he raped. There, it is talking about a woman he married.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question from Step 34. Each פסוק is talking about a different situation, so they do not really clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man married a woman, her daughters and granddaughters are forbidden to him. If he only raped her, that relationship does not forbid her descendants who are not his own children. So the 'permitted' verse speaks about אונסין, and the 'forbidden' verse speaks about נשואין.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there. A short way of saying each source is talking about a different case.
Rape, meaning a relationship forced on a woman without marriage.
Marriage, a full legal marriage to the woman.

steps.whatToRemember: Marrying a woman makes her daughters and granddaughters forbidden. Raping her does not, unless they are the man's own children. This is the teaching of רבא that the גמרא used in Step 33.
steps.confusionAlert: This does NOT mean a man's own daughter or granddaughter from an אנוסה is permitted. She is still his own family. Only the woman's other descendants, who are not from him, are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא brought רבא's teaching in Step 33 to show that a sister born to an אנוסה cannot be excluded from the איסור. A child from an אנוסה is still treated as real family to her father.

phrases.english: Here, it is speaking of rape;
phrases.notes: This is the verse that implied the woman's granddaughters are permitted.

phrases.english: there, it is speaking of marriage.
phrases.notes: This is the verse that forbids a woman's granddaughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction רבא raised in Step 34. This completes the proof the גמרא brought in Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seemed to give opposite rulings about a woman's granddaughters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitting verse is about a woman he raped (אונסין). The forbidding verse is about a woman he married (נשואין).
